issues.legal_issue: A timely appeal from a decree in a single suit is not barred merely because a separate appeal from another decree based on the same judgment was filed late.
material_facts: One suit was tried and decided by one judgment, and the appellate court also disposed of the resulting appeals by one judgment.
Separate decrees were drawn up from that appellate judgment for different groups of defendants.
The plaintiffs filed one appeal in time and a second appeal late; the timely appeal impleaded all defendants and challenged the decision concerning the whole suit.
issues.conclusion: Separate appeals were not necessary, and the late filing of the second appeal did not make the timely appeal unmaintainable by res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: The determining factor is the matter in controversy, not the number of decrees. Res judicata arises only where there are two suits; a single judgment in a single suit does not become separate decisions merely because appeals bear different numbers or separate decrees were drawn. The Court applied Mst. Lachmi v. Mst. Bhuli and referred to Appa v. Kachai Bayyan Kutti; it rejected the approach taken in Jethmal v. Ranglal.

rule.if: appeal_from_single_suit and one_common_judgment_decides_the_matter and separate_decrees_drawn and timely_appeal_covers_entire_matter and another_appeal_filed_late

predicates.appeal_from_single_suit: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a single suit.
predicates.one_common_judgment_decides_the_matter: The matter was decided through one judgment in the suit and the ensuing appellate proceeding.
predicates.separate_decrees_drawn: Separate decrees were prepared despite the common judgment.
predicates.timely_appeal_covers_entire_matter: The appellant filed an appeal in time that challenged the decision concerning the whole matter and included all affected opposing parties.
predicates.another_appeal_filed_late: A separate appeal concerning another decree from the same judgment was filed after the limitation period.

issues.definition: When an appeal arises from a single suit decided by one common judgment, separate decrees and a late additional appeal do not bar a timely appeal that covers the entire matter.

issues.legal_issue: Conflicting judicial decisions on the appeal procedure constitute sufficient cause to grant relief from a filing delay.
material_facts: The appellant filed a separate appeal twenty-nine days after the limitation period had expired.
There was a conflict of decisions on whether separate appeals were required, both within the relevant High Court and among different High Courts in India.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong not to give the appellant the benefit of an extension of time under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 permits time to be extended where sufficient cause is shown. In the circumstances, conflicting judicial rulings on the procedural question justified giving the appellant that benefit; Mst. Lachmi v. Mst. Bhuli was applied, and Appa v. Kachai Bayyan Kutti was cited in support.

predicates.appeal_seeking_extension_of_time: The proceeding is an appeal in which the appellant seeks relief from a filing delay.
predicates.appeal_filed_late: The appellant filed the appeal after the applicable limitation period.
predicates.conflicting_decisions_on_procedure: Different courts had issued conflicting decisions on the procedural requirement relevant to filing the appeal.

issues.definition: When a late appeal seeks an extension and conflicting procedural decisions exist, the delay should be excused.
